initial_precision_evaluation.result: All seven cases produce appropriately scoped decisions: three concrete objections already covered by maintainer comments, four legitimate positive controls. No mandatory wording defect found.

suggested_refinements.suggestion: Explicitly distinguish observing wrappers that call the original method, and bounded lifecycle stimuli on a real bot, from replacing the production boundary. Mineflayer4099 is a concrete positive example.
suggested_refinements.reason: Prevents mechanical interpretation of the substituted-boundaries list as a ban on any direct emit or client.write wrapper.

limits: These are inspection-based skill usability/precision checks, not runtime tests.
The common reference itself includes the three negative exemplars and model positives, so this is a regression/precision exercise, not evidence of broad unseen-case generalization.
Merged142/4099 are historical controls; they are not pending review targets.

rows.head: bb782e746229a5cb9fdce7f4854f23309ac1b3b2
rows.boundary_decision: Keep local unit fixture; repair CI discovery and index-zero assertion
evidence: The fix changes channel-array lookup/removal and decoded payload dispatch. EventEmitter plus production injected plugin meaningfully exercises this local behavior. Existing declareCommandsTest has an injected EventEmitter client precedent.
The first test observes both removed and retained channel emissions and distinguishes the affected production behavior; packet encoding/network/server claims are not made.
CI runs npm run mochaTest -- -g ${{ matrix.mcVersion }}v. The new describe pluginChannels and its two it titles have no version label, so CI filters both out despite local Mocha discovery.

The second case listens on minecraft:unregister but emits example:only. Its received array stays empty even if example:only still dispatches. The last removed example channel is at index1 after minecraft:register removal; no observable assertion directly validates the initial index0 removal.

findings.request: Put the suite under supported version-labelled discovery or add an explicit CI unit-test run.
Observe the channel actually removed at index0, emit that payload, and also prove the retained neighbor still dispatches. Keep this as a focused unit test; no TCP rewrite required.

refined_precision_evaluation.conclusion: Refinement correctly prevents mandatory integration migrations for algorithm/local-dispatch claims while preserving concrete assertion/discovery requests.

peer_review.dedup: No equivalent prior finding; earlier Astra readiness is explicitly revised.
peer_review.assessment: Second inline is concrete and well supported. First inline combines valid CI exclusion with a potentially overbroad mandatory fixture replacement.
peer_review.reason: Channel registration/removal and decoded-event dispatch can be meaningfully unit-tested using EventEmitter; this is less obviously an integration-only behavior than bot actions. Exact head also contains an injected EventEmitter chat-plugin unit test. The channel codec still executes within the real plugin for typed channels. A no-op write is irrelevant when custom=false in all calls. CI exclusion and inaccurate index-zero assertion require repair regardless.
peer_review.recommendation: Keep vacuous-assertion and CI findings. Qualify real client/server route as integration regression guidance; allow a corrected focused unit case as supplementary evidence instead of imposing a blanket NMP plugin fixture ban.
peer_review.test_execution: No new execution. Independently traced code and read recorded fixed/mutated 2-pass runs.

peer_review.assessment: Repository-fit migration request has a real existing destination, but rationale risks misclassifying algorithm tests as fake integration.
peer_review.reason: Both disputed cases exercise actual AStar + production path postprocessing over real Block state objects. They compare raw vs processed coordinates, not packet initialization, controls, execution or server swim success. Calling pathfinder(bot) exposes the plugin closure but does not by itself turn an algorithm assertion into a lifecycle claim. Prior reported head/base negative controls also distinguish the bug.
peer_review.recommendation: Narrow to duplicate fixture maintenance/repository consistency if retaining requested migration; recognize existing tests as useful valid model evidence and do not make network initialization a general prerequisite for pure path algorithms.
peer_review.test_execution: Source inspection only; no fresh model run.

peer_review.dedup: Existing re-entry correctness request differs from this writer/observation issue; no duplicate found.
peer_review.reason: Tests explicitly claim packet status/order/sequence across versions but replace _client.write with a collector, so assertions never observe serialization or server-received fields. Review preserves useful local re-entry/listener assertions and limits the request to packet observations.

refinements_applied: Inspect overrides after real-bot setup, not just filename or initial createBot call.
Distinguish delegated observing wrappers and bounded lifecycle stimuli from replacing production paths.
Allow actual path algorithms exposed through plugins and NMP local decoded-dispatch unit tests.
Require successful protocol transitions to detect unexpected parser/connection errors; preserve expected malformed-packet tests.
